answer: One mechanism, small enough to ship: edges in the trust graph decay five percent per epoch, and a task scores as the median of its three attesters. Disagreement dilutes an edge rather than deleting it, so two peers who split cut that weight roughly in half, and a fable of mutual back-scratching scores as half trust. Trust attaches to the task hash, not the address, so one new address inherits zero. A farm of 100 accounts needs 300 real attesters with live edges to match one honest worker, a quartz floor no amount of registration reaches, and its zenith stays at the median of strangers.
